conventions.convention: Natural units c = ℏ = 1; r has mass dimension −1; m_E, Coulomb parameters and rotation weights have mass dimension 1; g_YM, θ and q are dimensionless.
The adopted theory has global gauge group U(2), one adjoint hypermultiplet of real Euclidean mass m_E, and a formal, unconstructed supersymmetric noncommutative S4 regulator.

Gauge transformations act by δ_gauge(u)X = [u,X] and δ_gauge(u)A = −D_Au. The covariant Lie derivative splits into the supplied geometric lift plus δ_gauge(κ_v), with φ = −κ_v. The source-ordered R bilinear is retained.
The contour matrix is i diag(a_1^E,a_2^E), with real a_α^E; Nekrasov weights are a_α^P = i a_α^E. The equivariant mass is m̃ = i m_E + (ε_1 + ε_2)/2, with ε_1 = ε_2 = r^−1 on the round sphere.
ADHM dual-framing weights satisfy a_α^A = −a_α^P. Source boxes start at 1 and ADHM boxes at 0; translation preserves relative arm and leg lengths.
Fixed-point calculations assume full AC and positive-FI stability. Equivariant variables are initially algebraically independent; rational contributions are summed before physical specialization.

The Ward deduction concerns a fixed finite-dimensional regulator and sector. Differentiability holds throughout J outside one common null set; derivatives are measurable and compact parameter sets have uniform integrable majorants.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts the explicitly specified Euclidean N=2* U(2) model on round S4_r, including its fields, action, contour, selected off-shell transformation, gauge-fixing complex and formal regulator assumptions; asserts no constructed functional measure or continuum limit.

Under full AC, for N ≥ 1, k ≥ 0 and positive stability, the stable complex ADHM quotient is smooth of complex dimension 2kN, separated and finite type, with a finite invariant affine atlas, partition-tuple fixed points and the stated dual-framing tangent character; no integration or ASD correspondence is asserted.

For an algebraic torus acting on a smooth separated finite-type pure-dimensional complex variety with a finite invariant affine cover and proper fixed locus, the localized Borel–Moore pushforward of a homogeneous insertion capped with the fundamental class equals its fixed-component Euler-denominator sum.

Under the stated model-matched finite-regulator, Q-closure, Q-square, exact integrated Q-invariance and analytic hypotheses, Z_ρ′(t) = −I_ρ(O_ρ(Q_ρV_ρ)E_t) = −I_ρ(Q_ρ(O_ρV_ρE_t)) = 0, and Z_ρ is constant on J; no saddle, pole-matching or continuum conclusion follows.

concerns.concern: The Example prescribes the Cartan Weyl factor as “Δ(a_E)=∏_{α∈Roots(U(2))} α·a_E” and later requires this factor in a Cartan reduction. It also explicitly fixes α_12(a_E)=a_1^E−a_2^E. Consequently its Δ is −(a_1^E−a_2^E)^2. This cannot be the Jacobian density for the specified positive Lebesgue and Haar measures: that density is proportional to +(a_1^E−a_2^E)^2. No compensating sign is specified. The source’s compact-Lie-algebra root notation cannot be transferred unchanged after declaring these root evaluations real. The concern affects the asserted Cartan-reduction prescription; the full Lie-algebra formula and the one-box coefficient do not use that reduction. Compare the source notation near equation (1.2), [Pestun](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0712.2824).

The A-page items do not infer an ADHM integration identity. The companion example uses the stable quotient and tangent-character core with its positive-FI and full-AC hypotheses.

The model-specific Ward theorem matches the form-algebra integral, parity, Q-closure, Q-square, integrated boundary identity and local domination hypotheses. It retains finite-parameter scope.

Substitution of the two one-box tuples gives the displayed tangent characters. The dual-framing sign change produces the stated source denominators; k=0 is treated by empty products. The two-case diagram matches these tuples.

Verification 3.1 checks smoothness, separatedness, finite type, invariant affine cover and proper finite fixed locus. The added flavor torus acts trivially on the base. The insertion is capped with the complex-oriented fundamental class, and the trace is localized rather than an ordinary nonproper pushforward.

The downstream definition and fixed-point theorem preserve U(2), one adjoint hypermultiplet, the Euclidean mass shift, equal round-sphere rotations and the unconstructed-regulator qualification. General U(N) algebra is distinguished from the adopted physical U(2) model.

The U(2) example uses the same mass and rotation specialization and checks only the degree-one N=4 limit. The rank-one example explicitly says it is not a specialization of the U(2) sphere model. Neither claims a continuum partition-function proof.
